question: Why do nurses write and share research reports?

options.A: To promote individual nurse researchers
options.B: To criticize current medical practices publicly
options.C: To fulfill hospital administrative requirements
options.D: To share findings and improve patient care

explanation: Research reports document clinical investigations primarily to communicate evidence that improves patient outcomes in practice. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h1)

question: Why do research reports use a strict, formal format?

options.A: To ensure clarity, objectivity, and reproducibility
options.B: To restrict reading access to senior researchers only
options.C: To hide methodological flaws from peer reviewers
options.D: To make the document look more professional and longer

explanation: A standardized format allows readers to easily locate specific information and replicate the study if needed. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h1)

question: In research writing, what does the word IMRAD stand for?

options.A: Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion
options.B: Investigation, Materials, Review, and Data
options.C: Initial, Measurement, Research, and Analysis
options.D: Interpretation, Management, Reporting, and Design

explanation: IMRAD is the standard organizational spine used across scientific and nursing research literature. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h2)

question: Where can a busy nurse quickly find a short summary of an entire research study?

options.A: The reference list
options.B: The methodology
options.C: The abstract
options.D: The appendices

explanation: The abstract provides a concise snapshot of the research problem, methods, results, and conclusions. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h2)

question: At what point in the writing process should you draft your study's abstract?

options.A: Before formulating the main research question
options.B: Immediately following the title selection
options.C: After completing the entire research report
options.D: At the same time as the literature review

explanation: Because the abstract summarizes every section, it can only be written accurately once the full study is finished. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h3)

question: What is the main job of the introduction section in a research paper?

options.A: To acknowledge funding sources and helpers
options.B: To establish the research gap and study purpose
options.C: To list the statistical software used for analysis
options.D: To provide a detailed summary of all raw data

explanation: The introduction frames the background context and explains why the current study is necessary. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h3)

question: How should a strong literature review present past studies?

options.A: Grouped exclusively by the author's last name
options.B: Listed chronologically from oldest to newest
options.C: Synthesized by themes and conceptual arguments
options.D: Summarized one by one in separate paragraphs

explanation: Synthesizing by themes shows how different studies relate to each other and highlights gaps in the literature. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h4)

question: Why do researchers include a literature review in their report?

options.A: To prove that previous researchers were wrong
options.B: To provide raw data for statistical testing
options.C: To increase the total word count of the report
options.D: To show familiarity with existing knowledge and gaps

explanation: The literature review contextualizes the new study within the broader body of established scientific knowledge. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h4)

question: What is the main reason for writing a detailed methodology section?

options.A: To allow other researchers to replicate the study
options.B: To highlight the personal opinions of the author
options.C: To convince readers that the statistics are correct
options.D: To replace the need for an abstract summary

explanation: Transparency in methods ensures scientific validity by enabling replication and verification by peers. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h5)

question: Why must ethical considerations be clearly written in the methods section?

options.A: To explain how statistical bias was eliminated
options.B: To prove participant protection and institutional approval
options.C: To protect the researcher from financial liability
options.D: To fulfill bureaucratic requirements without real meaning

explanation: Documenting ethics confirms that human subjects were treated safely and rights were respected during the research. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h5)

question: What belongs in the results section of a research report?

options.A: Detailed critique of previous literature
options.B: Broad historical background of the topic
options.C: Objective findings and statistical outcomes
options.D: Personal opinions and clinical recommendations

explanation: The results section reports what was found without inserting the author's subjective interpretations or opinions. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h6)

question: How are qualitative research findings usually shown in the results section?

options.A: By listing demographic survey percentages only
options.B: Through complex numerical regression equations
options.C: Using direct participant quotes to support themes
options.D: Using randomized controlled trial flowcharts

explanation: Qualitative results rely on thematic text and verbatim quotes from participants to reflect their lived experiences. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of the discussion section in a report?

options.A: To introduce brand new research questions
options.B: To present raw numerical data tables
options.C: To interpret the meaning of the results
options.D: To list references in alphabetical order

explanation: The discussion makes sense of the findings, linking data back to clinical reality and prior literature. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h7)

question: Why should a researcher point out study limitations in the discussion?

options.A: To satisfy journal word count minimums
options.B: To prevent overgeneralization of the findings
options.C: To prove that the research was a complete failure
options.D: To eliminate the need for future studies

explanation: Transparency regarding weaknesses helps readers judge where and when the findings can safely be applied. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h7)

question: What should recommendations in a research report be based on?

options.A: Financial goals of the funding agency
options.B: The personal opinions of the lead author
options.C: General popular opinions in the hospital
options.D: The empirical findings of the study

explanation: Recommendations must arise logically from the data collected and analyzed during the research process. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h8)

question: How do conclusions differ from results in a research report?

options.A: Conclusions outline the step-by-step methodology
options.B: Conclusions contain raw numbers and statistical tests
options.C: Conclusions list participant quotes and interview transcripts
options.D: Conclusions synthesize the overarching meaning of the study

explanation: While results present data, conclusions provide the final overarching takeaway message of the investigation. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h8)

question: What is the purpose of an appendix at the end of a research report?

options.A: To list all bibliographic references cited in text
options.B: To house supplementary materials like questionnaires
options.C: To summarize the abstract in another language
options.D: To display financial sponsorship acknowledgments

explanation: Appendices keep bulky items like tools and consent forms available for review without disrupting the main text. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h9)

question: Which of these is a violation of academic integrity in research writing?

options.A: Citing peer-reviewed journal articles in the text
options.B: Using a standardized referencing style like APA
options.C: Acknowledging original authors for their ideas
options.D: Copying text word-for-word without quotation marks

explanation: Using another person's words without proper citation or quotation constitutes plagiarism, which violates academic integrity. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h9)

question: What is the main goal of sharing or disseminating a completed research report?

options.A: To archive the document permanently in a library
options.B: To prevent other nurses from studying the topic
options.C: To share findings so clinical staff can apply them
options.D: To fulfill university graduation criteria only

explanation: Dissemination ensures that new evidence reaches the wider healthcare community to improve patient care. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h10)

question: Why is peer review an important step before publishing a research paper?

options.A: It reduces the cost of printing the final journal
options.B: It guarantees that the study will win academic awards
options.C: It provides expert critique to improve quality and validity
options.D: It eliminates the need for any editing by the author

explanation: Independent reviewers evaluate the manuscript to catch errors and suggest improvements before public release. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h10)
